translations.answer: The maintainer confirmed that the function calculates the total mass moment of a rigid body tree, with the origin of the frame located at the center of mass (CoM) and the axes aligned with the world frame. Subsequent follow-up confirmed that the time variation of linear momentum also follows the same convention. When time derivatives are required, the function computeCentroidalMomentumTimeVariation should be called. Since the original thread did not provide examples of vector elements or numerical values, the implementation should still verify the target version documentation.
translations.applicability: Applies to the Pinocchio computeCentroidalMomentum and computeCentroidalMomentumTimeVariation functions; the output arrangement and units still adhere to the target version.
translations.credibility.rationale: There is engineering record for the environment, processing steps, and results, but formal cross-verification or independent replication is lacking.
translations.details.attempts.0: The maintainer directly confirmed the function definition, frame, and time derivative interface.
translations.details.attempts.1: The original author clarified the base modeling with fixed mechanical arms, cart-pendulum, and JointModelPlanar mobile base gradually.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: Recorded the origin and axis direction of the centroidal momentum frame: origin at CoM, axes aligned with the world frame.
translations.details.diagnostics.1: Checked whether the model's base has actual generalized coordinates; do not equate 'no FreeFlyer' with a fixed base.
translations.details.diagnostics.2: Distinguished between the moment of a stationary fixed base and the moment of a base with planar or prismatic degrees of freedom.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: Explicitly model the corresponding degrees of freedom in the base for mobile base contributions to system momentum; the thread confirmed that JointModelPlanar is a valid modeling entry for mobile plane bases.
translations.details.environments.0: 2020–2022 Pinocchio C++ API; original post did not provide specific version, URDF, or numerical test.
translations.details.limits.0: The thread did not provide the order of vector elements, units, or numerical examples for linear/angular momentum; these should be verified against the target version API documentation and tests.
translations.details.limits.1: The maintainer's final reply to the URDF and buildModel(..., JointModelPlanar()) was very brief; this card does not expand it to any model being numerically equivalent.
translations.details.limits.2: This thread does not discuss external forces, contact switching, or the time derivative of the centroidal momentum matrix.
translations.details.outcomes.0: The original author confirmed that computeCentroidalMomentum's definition addressed the question and expressed understanding after discussing base modeling.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: What frame does computeCentroidalMomentum return, and how is its time derivative obtained?
translations.details.problem_statements.1: How are the moments of inertia of fixed base, prismatic cart, and planar mobile base incorporated into the centroidal dynamics?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Momentum control should be used in real machines only after independent momentum and force/moment balance checks for frame, units, and base degrees of freedom to avoid erroneous constraints leading to large contact forces.
translations.details.symptoms.0: The caller is uncertain whether computeCentroidalMomentum corresponds to the Orin, Goswami, and Lee 2013 human body centroidal momentum.
translations.details.symptoms.1: The caller further questions whether the cart-pendulum or fixed mechanical arm base moments are included when no explicit JointModelFreeFlyer is used.
translations.source.locator: Pinocchio #1252 comment 650976642 confirms definition, frame, and time derivative interface; comment 651815897 confirms the original author; comment 1051564222 confirms the same for linear momentum.
translations.source.title: Expression of linear and angular momentum in Pinocchio computeCentroidalMomentum and its base modeling boundaries
